claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to consider for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help you with Alex's eligibility.

To assess whether you can claim Child Benefit for Alex, I need to gather some details about his circumstances.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he live with someone else (such as the other parent, a grandparent, or in care)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Before I make my final assessment, I need to understand the full situation a bit better. Let me read the relevant guidance on Child Benefit eligibility when a child lives with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the guidance, since Alex lives with his mum (someone else), there are specific rules that apply. 

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or payments towards his accommodation)?** If so, roughly how much are you contributing per week or month?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out with things like clothes and bits and pieces for school. I give about £10 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

Now I have one more important question to make sure I have the full picture:

**Is Alex's mum (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules, I can provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time. 

Here's why: While you do make financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (£10 per week for clothes and school items), the fundamental rule is that **only one person can receive Child Benefit for a single child**. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim it.

Your contributions are valuable and show you're financially supporting Alex, but they cannot be used to claim Child Benefit while someone else is already receiving it for him.

**If things change in the future** — for example, if his mum stops claiming — you could potentially claim for Alex based on your contributions to his upkeep. If that happens, you'd want to contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss your situation.

Is there anything else I can help clarify?

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally continue to receive Child Benefit for more than 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else if you make contributions to their upkeep. However, the key rule is that only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim it for the same child. The rules state: 'Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child.' While your weekly contributions of £10 towards Alex's clothes, school items and upkeep would normally help sustain eligibility beyond the initial 8 weeks, this is only relevant if you were the one claiming. Since his mum is the current claimant, you are not eligible to receive Child Benefit for Alex.
